children: India's National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) has accepted bids worth $750 million through a debut U.S. dollar denominated bond with 10-year maturity, at cutoff which was 25 basis points lower than initial guidance, two merchant bankers said on Thursday.
NaBFID sold the bonds at a spread of 105 basis points above U.S. Treasury, and the coupon works out to be 6.1220%, sufficiently lower than the initial guidance of 130 bps.
The Indian financial institution received bids worth over $2 billion indicating strong demand for the first-time issuer.
CreditSights had expected the pricing at a spread of 105 bps, but said the fair value is around 97 bps

The bonds have been sold under the discounted swap window, after the Reserve Bank of India allowed banks and state-run companies to raise funds overseas and access a subsidised hedging facility, lowering the cost of managing currency risk since June.
NaBFID is targeting a total fundraise of $4 billion before end of 2026
Of this, the infra lender has already raised $850 million through external commercial borrowing in August
The institution had raised $125 million via dollar loan in March, which was its debut borrowing in the offshore market.
Apart from NaBFID, Power Finance Corp is other state-run entity that has tapped the dollar bond route to raise funds
Meanwhile, lenders have raised $13 billon since June under the swap facility.
